audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty framing was generic and the page referred to Ahri as 'he'/'him' in tldr, tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.early and breakdown.feeding.
audit.why: Ahri is female; the real difficulty driver is the 970-range Q against Annie's 625 Q and 600 W, not an unnamed 'setup-spell dependency'.
audit.corrected: Even (5.5/10): Ahri out-ranges Annie in the poke phase, Annie wins any exchange she opens with a stocked Pyromania stun.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[N].side was 'Skill' on all seven rows while content win[] and the packet levelChart read Skill/Skill/Skill/Annie/Annie/Ahri/Ahri.
audit.why: The two layers render the same level-chart row; four rows disagreed, so the page answered 'who wins Level 6' twice differently.
audit.corrected: full phases[3..6].side set to Annie/Annie/Ahri/Ahri to match content win[3..6] and the packet chart; ratings and whys re-grounded to the same story.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ability interactions were unnamed and two fields said Ahri bursts through Annie's 'passive shield'. Annie's passive is Pyromania (a stun), the shield is Molten Shield (E).
audit.why: Riot text: Pyromania stuns after 4 spells; E 'Grants Annie or an ally a shield'. Charm 'instantly stopping movement abilities' — it cancels dashes, and it is a flat 12s at every rank. Spirit Rush has three casts on 140/120/100s. Fox-Fire is 9/8/7/6/5s. Ahri's Q deals true damage on the return.
audit.corrected: Named Charm's 12s flat cooldown and dash-cancel, Fox-Fire's rank scaling, Spirit Rush's three charges, and corrected 'passive shield' to Molten Shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: Essence Theft sustain was never mentioned; no Grievous Wounds timing anywhere on the page.
audit.why: brief.missingInteractions flags needs-antiheal: Ahri heals off 9 minions and off takedowns, which decides extended poke wars.
audit.corrected: breakdown.feeding and ahead now name Essence Theft and Grievous Wounds.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns was a generic three-bullet template and dosFull[2].d called Charm a 'fifteen-second' cooldown.
audit.why: Charm is 12 seconds at all ranks.
audit.corrected: Rewrote cooldowns around Charm 12s, Fox-Fire 9->5s, Spirit Rush 140s rank 1.

edits.before: Hold the four-stack glow and watch him orbit at max range — a stocked Annie controls the lane by standing there.
edits.after: Hold the four-stack glow and watch her orbit at 970 Q range — a stocked Annie zones by standing there, Charm or not.

edits.before: Tibbers online — Flash-R-W-Q deletes most mids from full health. The lane is now a geometry problem about your Flash range.
edits.after: Tibbers online — Flash-R-W-Q deletes her from full. Charm is 12s flat; go on the miss, while Spirit Rush is still a 140s ult.

edits.before: Luden's/Stormsurge spike: the stun-burst math kills through Doran's defenses. Stock, walk forward, win.
edits.after: Her Shadowflame spike outranges yours — 970 Q against your 625, and Spirit Rush leaves before the bear lands.

edits.before: Late Annie flips fights with one button: flash-Tibbers the clump, peel with the bear, and re-stock off the chaos.
edits.after: Three Spirit Rush charges on a 100s ult dodge your 600-range R — you need Flash or a team's CC to land the bear.

edits.before: A burst duel where your combo is point-and-click — stock the stun and his setup-spell dependency becomes the whole gap.
edits.after: A burst duel where your combo is point-and-click — stock the stun and her 12s Charm dependency becomes the whole gap.

edits.before: Ahri wins by landing Charm, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Ahri wins by out-ranging you 970 to 625, taking true damage off every Q return, and charming your step-up.

edits.before: At four stacks: walk forward, Q-stun, W, auto, walk away re-stacking off the wave — a guaranteed chunk he answered with nothing.
edits.after: At four stacks: walk forward, Q-stun, W, auto, walk away re-stacking off the wave — a chunk her 7s Q cannot answer back.

edits.before: Spending the stocked stun on wave-clear with his engage loaded — unstacked Annie is the most killable mage in the lane.
edits.after: Spending the stocked stun on wave-clear with her Charm up — unstacked Annie has no answer to Charm into Fox-Fire burst.

edits.before: Ahead, shrink the lane: hold the glow, zone Ahri off CS by existing, and Flash-Tibbers the recovery attempt — fed Annie ends games at 20.
edits.after: Ahead, shrink the lane: hold the glow, starve Essence Theft by zoning her off CS, and Flash-Tibbers the recall attempt she tries to make.

edits.before: Farm refunds, stack quietly, and hold the glow — pre-6 Annie wins by threat, not action. The lane is a hostage negotiation.
edits.after: Farm refunds, stack quietly, hold the glow — her Q costs 55 mana and yours refunds on the kill, so the mana war is yours before six.

edits.before: Post-6 every fight inside Flash range is yours to start: stock, hover the river, and Flash-Tibbers the first clump that forgets you exist.
edits.after: Post-6 every fight inside Flash range is yours to start, but Spirit Rush holds three charges — force one out with a W before you commit the bear.

edits.before: - Ahri Charm: matchup-defining — The charm starts every kill pattern — stay behind minions while it is up. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E Molten Shield like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Charm is 12s flat at every rank and stops movement abilities — stay behind minions while it is up, step up on the miss. - Fox-Fire falls from 9s to 5s by rank 5; Charm is still the gate. - Spirit Rush is 140s at rank 1 — longer than Tibbers.

edits.before: If Ahri opens the score, reset expectations and respect Charm doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with Q refunds and stay relevant through stocked-stun threat.
edits.after: If Ahri opens the score her Essence Theft heal makes a poke war unwinnable — buy Grievous Wounds, farm with Q refunds, and stay relevant on stocked-stun threat alone.

edits.before: Carry through the one button — Flash-Tibbers on two is a won fight; your whole game is engineering the radius.
edits.after: Carry by punishing the 100s Spirit Rush: once its three charges are spent she is a 550-range mage inside your 600 Tibbers radius.

edits.before: You are one button from a won fight all game: flash-R the carry pair, peel with the bear, stun the second wave. Stack management IS positioning.
edits.after: She holds three Spirit Rush charges to dodge your R — bait one with W, then Flash-R the clump. Stack management IS positioning; arrive glowing.

edits.before: Ahri burns Charm on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Ahri burns Charm on nothing — take the twelve-second invitation.

edits.before: That’s Ahri’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Three stacks is no stun — her 12s Charm outlasts a rebuild you started.

edits.before: Track Ahri’s Charm: The charm starts every kill pattern — stay behind minions while it is up. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Charm: 12s flat, blocked by minions, and it cancels dashes. Stay behind the wave while it is up; step up on the miss.

edits.before: Even trading window — neither champion has landed a game-defining CC yet, so poke exchanges roughly cancel out
edits.after: Her Q reaches 970 to your 625, but it costs 55 mana and yours refunds on a kill — the mana war cancels the range gap

edits.before: Same logic holds a level later: both kits are still poke-only with no follow-up burst available
edits.after: Level 2 W is a clearing cone that also counts a stack; her Fox-Fire is still on a 9s cooldown here

edits.before: Level 3 stays even because neither Charm nor stun has a big enough combo behind it to flip a trade decisively
edits.after: Level 3 evens: your E shield eats Fox-Fire while stacking Pyromania, but Charm still starts her kill pattern

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are a poke stalemate — both of you are throwing skillshots (her Q, your unshielded autos) without a follow-up, so the lane is even until someone lands a clean stun or Charm to open a real trade.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are a poke stalemate — her 970-range Q outranges your 625, but yours refunds mana on a last hit, so she burns 55 a throw while you farm free and tick Pyromania toward a stocked stun.

edits.before: Once Ahri finishes a mobility or burst item she reclaims the fight — Spirit Rush both dodges your stun angle and repositions her for a follow-up Charm, and with Void Staff or Shadowflame she can delete you through your passive shield before Tibbers even lands a hit.
edits.after: Once Ahri finishes Shadowflame or Void Staff she reclaims the fight — Spirit Rush holds three charges to dodge your 600-range R and reposition for a follow-up Charm, and her burst goes through Molten Shield before Tibbers lands a hit. Bait a dash with W first.

edits.before: Ahri's Void Staff or Shadowflame lets her burst you through your passive shield the moment she lands Charm, and her Spirit Rush escape means you can't punish overextensions anymore.
edits.after: Ahri's Void Staff or Shadowflame bursts through Molten Shield the moment Charm lands, and Spirit Rush's three charges on a 120s cooldown mean you cannot punish her overextensions.

edits.before: Ahri scales into a mobile burst mage who can dodge your stun with Spirit Rush dashes and reset fights with true damage on low-HP targets; your all-in becomes a one-shot-or-nothing coinflip.
edits.after: Ahri scales into a mobile burst mage who dodges your stun with three Spirit Rush dashes and chips you with true damage on every Q return; your all-in becomes a one-shot-or-nothing coinflip.
